changeSet.author: agimate
changeSet.comment:
OAuth for connector instances (docs/decisions/mcp-oauth.md). Only what has to be searched or shown without decrypting the secret becomes a column: the tokens themselves, the issuer, the AS endpoints and the granted scope stay inside the connection's secret.
oauth_expires_at is deliberately out of the secret even though it travels with the token: inside the encrypted blob «who needs refreshing» could be answered neither by a query nor by the UI, and every background check would have to decrypt everything. NULL means «unknown» (the AS sent no expires_in), never «expired» — otherwise the job would refresh on a schedule that follows from nothing.

changeSet.author: agimate
changeSet.comment:
Multi-account support for MCP: two connections to one server must coexist, so uniqueness of (connector_code, user_id, sub_code) has to go. It cannot simply be dropped — for telegram a second connection to the same bot silently steals webhook delivery from the first — so the rule becomes data instead of code: exclusive_sub_code repeats sub_code where a second instance of the same account is harmful and stays NULL where multiple accounts are legitimate (NULLs never collide on a unique index in PostgreSQL). Filled by ConnectionService.create from IntegrationConnectorHandler.allowsMultipleInstances().
The alternative — «connector_code <> 'mcp'» inside the index — rots on the second multi-instance connector; a check in application code loses the race between two parallel creates. Backfill and the drop of the old index live in this one changeSet on purpose: between two changeSets there would be a window with no uniqueness at all.
changeSet.sql: UPDATE connections SET exclusive_sub_code = sub_code WHERE connector_code <> 'mcp';
